clue.text: Flood stopped wild beast returning

parts.note: something that has stopped is over, finished

indicators.note: returning tells us the beast's name is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: a wolf is a wild beast of the forest

explanation.surface: A flood was halted when a wild animal went back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopped' reads as part of the flood's story, but it is the adjective for finished; 'returning' signals the reversal of the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Water spilling over its banks or rim is a flood.

clue.text: Otherwise, has left vital energy source

parts.note: or means otherwise, as in hurry or you'll miss it
someone who has left is gone

explanation.surface: Advice that if you don't act, your vitality will have vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: Wilhelm Reich claimed this was a universal life force.
explanation.definitionFit: Reich's supposed universal life force was a source of vital energy.

clue.text: Raptors decapitating hounds

indicators.note: decapitating means cutting off the head, so the first letter of the hounds goes

parts.note: beagles are hunting hounds

explanation.surface: Birds of prey are taking the heads off dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Large birds of prey are raptors.

clue.text: Doting on fish — it's touching

parts.note: fond means doting, loving
a ling is a long cod-like sea fish

explanation.surface: Being devoted to fish is rather sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touching' looks like 'moving', but it is caressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Caressing someone is touching them lovingly.

clue.text: Smelly and has nothing on top

indicators.note: on means above in a down entry, so the zero sits over the other piece

parts.note: O is the letter shaped like zero, nothing
a lid is a top, as on a jar

explanation.surface: Something reeks and is not wearing anything on its head.
explanation.definitionFit: Olid is a rare word meaning foul-smelling, rank.

clue.text: Spring vegetable?

definitions.meaning: to spring up is to shoot or grow, as a seedling does
a Brussels green, the small cabbage-like bud eaten at Christmas

explanation.surface: A question about some greens grown in springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to shoot up; as a noun it is the small green Brussels vegetable.

clue.text: Pea soup everyone rejected for something fried

indicators.note: soup suggests ingredients stirred into a mixture, so the letters are rearranged
rejected means turned back, so the word for everyone is written backwards

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: Nobody wanted the pea soup, so a fry-up was made instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soup' rearranges PEA into PAE; 'rejected' turns ALL into LLA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish rice dish is cooked in a wide shallow frying pan.

clue.text: Bird takes flight, gripping on it somehow, with something fang-like

indicators.note: gripping means holding inside, so the second scrambled group sits within the first
takes flight suggests scattering, so the bird's letters are rearranged

parts.note: the dodo is the extinct flightless bird

indicators.note: somehow means arranged in some other way, so on and it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird flies off while clutching something that looks like a tooth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes flight' scrambles the bird and 'somehow' scrambles the two short words; 'gripping' puts the second group inside the first. Ironic, as the dodo could not fly.
explanation.definitionFit: Odontoid means toothlike, from the Greek for tooth, so it resembles a fang.

clue.text: Learnt to switch to easy-going attitude

indicators.note: switch means the letters change places with one another

explanation.surface: Someone learned to change to a relaxed outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switch' rearranges LEARNT TO; 'to easy-going attitude' reads as the result, with 'attitude' part of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A forbearing, permissive person is relaxed and easy-going.

clue.text: Caper after the carriage? Great!

indicators.note: after places the caper behind the carriage in the answer

parts.note: a gig is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage
an antic is a playful caper or prank

explanation.surface: Someone frolics behind a coach and exclaims how splendid it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enormous is great in size.

clue.text: Install different device and see thief bowled over

indicators.note: bowled over means knocked head over heels, so the word for the thief is turned back to front

parts.note: a looter is a thief who plunders

explanation.surface: A workshop is refitted and a burglar gets knocked down in the process.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowled over' turns LOOTER backwards; 'and see' only joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip again with new tools or machinery is to fit a different device.

clue.text: Speak to a head of department and come into line

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the following word is used

parts.note: soldiers dress when they align themselves in ranks

explanation.surface: An employee talks to their departmental boss and falls into step.
explanation.walkthrough: In military drill, to dress is to line up.
explanation.definitionFit: To address someone is to speak to them.

clue.text: First born led off — has one eye but cannot see

definitions.text: has one eye but cannot see

indicators.note: First places the word for born at the front, before the scrambled letters

parts.note: née, French for born, introduces a woman's maiden name

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of led are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: The eldest child was led away, one-eyed and blind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First born' looks like an eldest child; it is the French maiden-name marker placed first, with 'off' scrambling the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sewing pin has an eye for thread yet no sight, a classic riddle.

clue.text: Tailored — tailored to fit a big admirer

indicators.note: tailored to fit means altered and reshaped, so the letters of the first word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A suit is altered so a devoted fan can wear it.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Tailored' is the fodder; the repeated 'tailored to fit' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A worshipper of idols, by extension anyone who adores someone excessively.

clue.text: Rape he'd pulled out, planting this instead

indicators.note: pulled out suggests the letters are uprooted and scattered

parts.note: he'd is he had, giving the letters HED

explanation.surface: A gardener uprooted oilseed rape and sowed another shrub in its place.
explanation.walkthrough: Rape is the oilseed crop, here a plant; 'pulled out' rearranges RAPE HED.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a shrub genus, the source of ephedrine, that a gardener might plant.

clue.text: Rise and nip out, then take a deep breath

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Get up and pop outside, then fill your lungs with air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges RISE and NIP together.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhale is the literal, older sense of breathing in.

clue.text: One might meet him if sent back north more than once

indicators.note: sent back means the little word if is written in reverse order
more than once means the abbreviation for north is used twice

explanation.surface: A riddle about meeting someone if you keep heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns IF into FI; 'more than once' doubles the N. Heading north repeatedly could take you to Finland, where you might meet a native.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Finland is someone you might well meet in the far north.

clue.text: It's June in no time at all, for these insects

definitions.text: It's June in no time at all, for these insects

parts.words: It's June in no time at all, for these insects
parts.note: read as a statement that one spring month passes swiftly, as time does, before the next arrives, describing short-lived insects

explanation.surface: Time flies, and summer arrives before the bugs know it.
explanation.walkthrough: May flies, and it is soon June: the insects famously live only a day or so.
explanation.definitionFit: These insects with very short adult lives are named after the spring month.

clue.text: Over a thousand counted out — here's written proof?

indicators.note: Over means covering, so the scrambled word goes round the thousand
out signals that the letters of counted are rearranged

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: More than a thousand were tallied and a paper record exists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges COUNTED into DOCUENT, placed around M.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper record serves as written evidence.

clue.text: Life's aim? Could be!

indicators.note: Could be says the letters might form another word when rearranged

parts.note: the possessive gives its letters LIFES

explanation.surface: Musing on whether one's purpose in life is a household with children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' rearranges LIFES and AIM; the whole clue also suggests raising households is life's purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising households of children is often called life's purpose.

clue.text: Before long some clean ones will be needed

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the following words is taken, the run of letters spanning them

explanation.surface: Soon we will need a few fresh ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old word meaning soon or shortly.

clue.text: She's furious with the boy — sacking will follow

indicators.note: furious suggests wild agitation, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: she's is she is, giving the letters SHES
Ian is a typical boy's name in crosswords

explanation.surface: A woman is livid with a lad, and he is about to be fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'furious' rearranges SHES into HESS, followed by IAN. Hessian is coarse jute cloth used for sacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse jute cloth used to make sacks is called sacking.

clue.text: Short way to get bread — don't hurry

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
a roll is a small loaf of bread

explanation.surface: Advice for walking to the bakery at a leisurely pace.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble or saunter is to walk without hurrying.

clue.text: Zodiac sign incorporating a formidable woman

indicators.note: incorporating means taking in, so the single letter goes inside the sign

parts.note: Virgo is the sign of the Virgin

explanation.surface: A star sign that includes a fearsome female.
explanation.definitionFit: A domineering, bad-tempered woman is called a virago.

clue.text: Cat gets the bird — the whole bird

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A cat catches a bird and eats it entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: Each half is a creature; together they are one small bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A small songbird, especially a blue tit, called a tomtit.

clue.text: Experiencing palpitations when you take a plane round state?

indicators.note: round means the travelling word goes around the word for state

parts.note: to fly is to travel by plane
to utter is to state or say aloud

explanation.surface: Someone gets the jitters whenever they board an aeroplane to go round a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a country or US state but is the verb, to say.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart that flutters is beating irregularly, as in palpitations.

clue.text: I want the lot! Look out! It's my psychic urge

indicators.note: out here means outside: the word for look sits on the outside of the other letters

parts.note: lo, as in lo and behold, means look
at an auction you bid when you want the lot on sale

explanation.surface: A greedy shout of 'I want everything!' followed by a warning, explained as a mental drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' wraps the exclamation round the other pieces; 'the lot' is an auction lot, not everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Freudian theory names the psychic energy of sexual desire this way.

clue.text: The fish market always stocks salmon

indicators.note: stocks means holds within, so the answer is found running across the words

explanation.surface: The fishmonger's stall always has salmon on sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The fish' is surface dressing; keta is a Pacific salmon.
explanation.definitionFit: The chum salmon of the Pacific is called keta.

clue.text: Cerium in the same place, beef in cold storage

indicators.note: in means the cerium symbol goes inside the abbreviation

parts.note: ib. (ibidem) is the scholarly abbreviation for in the same place
Ce is the chemical symbol for cerium
an ox is a beef animal

explanation.surface: A chemical and some beef kept together in a fridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A refrigerator or cool box is a container for cold storage.

clue.text: Is the harassed worker lacking confidence?

indicators.note: harassed suggests being harried and disturbed, so the two short words are rearranged

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: Is the overworked employee feeling unsure?
explanation.walkthrough: 'harassed' rearranges IS THE into HESIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unsure and wavering lacks confidence.

clue.text: It's for the bench to decide

definitions.meaning: a long wooden seat with a high back
to resolve or determine a matter

explanation.surface: It is up to the judges to make the ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-backed wooden seat is one sense; to resolve a dispute is the other.

clue.text: Get through with wine examined at the border

parts.note: to pass is to get through
port is a fortified Portuguese wine

explanation.surface: Someone smuggles some wine through customs.
explanation.definitionFit: A travel document is checked by officials at frontiers.
